tool_analysis:
1) Step Analysis / What the recorded steps accomplish:
- Navigate from about:blank to the Magento admin customers grid URL.
- Log into Magento admin with username=admin and password=password123.
- Land on the Manage Customers grid.
- Open a specific customer edit page by clicking the per-row "Edit" link (customer id 192 in the recording).
- On the customer edit page:
  - Switch to the Account Information tab via its label, not via #customer_info_tabs_account.
  - Edit account-level fields: group and first name (and potentially others) via stable name-based selectors.
  - Switch to the Addresses tab and edit an address field in the inline "Edit Customer's Address" form.
  - Switch to the Newsletter tab and toggle the "Subscribed to Newsletter?" checkbox.
  - Click "Save Customer" to persist changes.

2) Task Definition / Purpose of the tool:
Create a reusable tool that, given a customer ID and new field values, does the following in Magento 1.9 admin:
- Navigates directly to the Manage Customers grid and then to that customer's edit page via the grid per-row Edit link (demonstrating the grid interaction requirement).
- Edits specified Account Information fields (first name, last name, email, group, website ID).
- Optionally edits a primary address field (second street line) in the Addresses tab.
- Optionally sets newsletter subscription state in the Newsletter tab.
- Saves the customer using the visible "Save Customer" button.
Crucially, it must avoid the previously failing selector #customer_info_tabs_account and instead rely on robust name-based or text-based selectors and/or the recorded element hashes.

3) Action Plan / To-do list of necessary steps:
A. Navigation & Login
- Step A1: navigation to admin customer grid URL /index.php/admin/customer/.
- Step A2: input username into the login username field (element_hash 3597a5c5e6).
- Step A3: input password into the login password field (element_hash 1c47a5217e).
- Step A4: click the Login button (element_hash 6831836d17).

B. Open customer edit page from grid (per-row Edit link)
- Step B1: Ensure we are on Manage Customers grid (navigation to same URL again is safe / idempotent).
- Step B2 (agentic): Locate the grid row corresponding to the target customer ID and click its "Edit" action link in the Action column (because the demonstrated click used index 105 but that index is row-order dependent; we need a dynamic strategy). This is where an agent step is appropriate.

C. Account Information tab: edit account fields
- Step C1: Click the "Account Information" tab via its text label (element_hash 15c034811f).
- Step C2: Input new First Name into the First Name field (element_hash c97ae058b0, and we know from analysis it corresponds to name="account[firstname]").
- Step C3: Optionally select the customer Group via select_change on the Group field (element_hash 3ea20d8dee; text like "General", "Wholesale", "VIP Member", etc.).

D. Addresses tab: edit address field
- Step D1: Click the "Addresses" tab (element_hash e10247917d).
- Step D2: Input address line 2 (e.g., suite) into the appropriate Street Address secondary input (element_hash 8a7bd934fa).

E. Newsletter tab: toggle subscription
- Step E1: Click the "Newsletter" tab (element_hash 377d4eed8b).
- Step E2: Click the "Subscribed to Newsletter?" checkbox (element_hash dd8c60e0a0). For simplicity we will treat the desired state as a boolean input and, because we lack direct read-state tooling, we will click it conditionally via an agent or simply click once assuming idempotent expectation. However, since tools have no conditionals, we instead make the action unconditional and document that callers should ensure the desired toggle pattern. To better respect desired state, we will use an agent step to set the checkbox to the requested boolean.

F. Save the customer
- Step F1: Click the "Save Customer" button (element_hash f224d73626).

4) Variable Identification / Input parameters:
Essential dynamic inputs based on observed DOM:
- customer_id (string, required): which row to open via the grid Edit link (pattern /admin/customer/edit/id/{id}/). Tool must demonstrate grid-based navigation instead of direct URL.
- account_firstname (string, optional): new First Name for Account Information (maps to account[firstname]).
- account_lastname (string, optional): new Last Name (account[lastname]) if provided.
- account_email (string, optional): new Email (account[email]) if provided.
- account_group (string, optional, enum ["General","Wholesale","VIP Member","Private Sales Member"]): new customer group; used in select_change on the Group select.
- account_website (string, optional, enum ["Admin","Main Website"]): Associate to Website; not explicitly interacted with in recording but documented in analysis; including as optional allows more completeness.
- address_street2 (string, optional): additional street line to input in address form (element_hash 8a7bd934fa), e.g., "Suite 500".
- newsletter_subscribed (bool, optional): desired subscription state; when provided, an agent step will ensure the checkbox state matches this value.

We do NOT parameterize login username/password since they are fixed by instructions (admin/password123).

5) Step Optimization / Simplifications and fixes:
- Avoid direct use of #customer_info_tabs_account, which failed previously. Instead, rely on:
  - Deterministic click using element_hash 15c034811f for Account Information tab.
  - Similar deterministic hashes for Addresses (e10247917d), Newsletter (377d4eed8b), checkbox (dd8c60e0a0), and Save Customer (f224d73626).
- Optimize navigation: directly navigate to /admin/customer/ once at the start, then use an agent step on the grid to click the appropriate Edit link using the customer ID. We will not directly navigate to /admin/customer/edit/id/{id}/ because the requirement explicitly wants a demonstration via grid Edit link.
- Replace brittle index-based operations with elementHash and/or agentic targeting when the index clearly depends on current row position (e.g., index 105 for an Edit link is not stable). For account and address fields, element hashes appear stable for this recording and are safer than inferred name attributes in this tool framework.
- Use a single final Save Customer click rather than multiple saves.
- Introduce one agent step to select the grid row Edit link for the given customer_id and one agent step to set newsletter_subscribed based on the desired boolean, since deterministic read-modify for checkboxes is not available via the basic actions.

Given this, the tool can be deterministic for all fields except:
- Selecting the correct row's Edit link (grid content is dynamic): requires agent reasoning.
- Ensuring newsletter checkbox matches a desired boolean: requires reading current state, so also best via agent.

The rest of the steps are deterministic interactions.
name: tool_view_edit_customer.v2
description: Open a specific Magento customer edit page from the customers grid via the per-row Edit link, modify key account, address, and newsletter fields, and save the customer, using robust selectors that avoid the failing #customer_info_tabs_account selector.

steps.description: Navigate to the Magento admin Manage Customers grid (login page will appear if not authenticated).
Enter the admin username into the login form username field.
Enter the admin password into the login form password field.
Submit the Magento admin login form by clicking the Login button.
Ensure we are on the Manage Customers grid after login (idempotent navigation).
On the Manage Customers grid, locate the row whose ID column equals the specified customer_id and click its 'Edit' link in the Action column to open the customer edit page.
steps.task: On the current Magento 'Manage Customers' grid page, find the table row where the ID column text equals {customer_id}, then within that row click the 'Edit' link in the Action column to open that customer's edit page.

steps.description: Click the 'Account Information' tab in the Customer Information tab bar to reveal account edit fields, using the recorded tab element.
If account_firstname is provided (non-empty), set the First Name field in Account Information. Leave unchanged if the value is empty; callers should pass current value if no change is desired.
If account_lastname is provided (non-empty), set the Last Name field in Account Information. Leave unchanged if the value is empty; callers should pass current value if no change is desired.
If account_email is provided (non-empty), set the Email field in Account Information. Leave unchanged if the value is empty; callers should pass current value if no change is desired.
If account_group is provided, select the corresponding customer group in the Group * dropdown in Account Information.
If account_website is provided, select the corresponding website in the Associate to Website * dropdown in Account Information.
Click the 'Addresses' tab to reveal the inline Edit Customer's Address form for the primary address.
If address_street2 is provided (non-empty), set the second line of the street address in the Edit Customer's Address form.
Click the 'Newsletter' tab in the Customer Information tab bar to reveal newsletter subscription controls.
Ensure the 'Subscribed to Newsletter?' checkbox in the Newsletter tab matches the desired newsletter_subscribed state (if provided).
steps.task: Within the currently open Newsletter tab of the Magento customer edit page, locate the checkbox labeled 'Subscribed to Newsletter?'. If newsletter_subscribed is true, ensure the checkbox is checked; if newsletter_subscribed is false, ensure it is unchecked. Use its label and surrounding 'Newsletter Information' section as context.

steps.description: Click the 'Save Customer' button to submit all changes to the customer record.

input_schema.name: customer_id
input_schema.description: Numeric customer ID to open from the Manage Customers grid via its per-row 'Edit' link (corresponds to /admin/customer/edit/id/{customer_id}/).

input_schema.name: account_firstname
input_schema.description: Optional new first name for the customer (Account Information > First Name *).

input_schema.name: account_lastname
input_schema.description: Optional new last name for the customer (Account Information > Last Name *).

input_schema.name: account_email
input_schema.description: Optional new email address for the customer (Account Information > Email *).

input_schema.name: account_group
input_schema.description: Optional customer group to assign in Account Information > Group *.

input_schema.name: account_website
input_schema.description: Optional website association to set in Account Information > Associate to Website *.

input_schema.name: address_street2
input_schema.description: Optional second line of the street address to input in the inline Edit Customer's Address form (e.g., 'Suite 500').

input_schema.name: newsletter_subscribed
input_schema.description: If provided, desired state of the 'Subscribed to Newsletter?' checkbox in the Newsletter tab (true=subscribed, false=unsubscribed).
